today.h: Brent at $116.72 and the 10Y Back at 5%: a 653-Point Hole in the Dow
today.d: October's flash PMI put selling-price inflation at a four-year high while Brent settled 3.1% higher at $116.72, pushing the 10Y back to 5.00%: the S&P fell 0.52%, the Dow 1.23%, and the Nasdaq only 0.20% as the chip complex found a floor.
today.c1: The barrel set the price of almost everything else on Friday. Brent's December contract settled $3.55, or 3.1%, higher at $116.72 — its highest close since 29 April, after a $117.45 session high — as Houthi strikes hit Saudi airports and Aramco sites and the Wall Street Journal reported that Tehran has warned it will strike airports, pipelines and telecoms in neighbouring Gulf states if US-Israeli air operations resume. The S&P 500 fell 0.52% to 7,623.68 (-39.75 points), 2.50% below its 10/6 record; the Dow dropped 652.82 points, or 1.23%, to 52,215.16; the Nasdaq lost only 0.20% to 25,955.34 because semiconductor and memory shares stopped falling. The October flash PMI turned the oil move into an inflation story rather than a demand story: the composite slipped to 57.6 from 58.4, but the selling-price index rose to 59.8, the highest since August 2022, and the 10Y gave back 4bp of Thursday's 17bp rally to 5.00% on the Treasury curve, with the 2Y at 4.69% and the 30Y at 5.33%. Gold settled 1.3% lower at $4,007.90 after trading down to $3,975.23, its first print below $4,000 since mid-July; the dollar added 0.18%, bitcoin was flat at $81.3k and the VIX rose 2.2% to 19.45.
today.c4:
• The transmission ran through the rate, not the economy: Brent +3.1% and selling prices at a four-year high put the 10Y back at 5.00%, and the rate-sensitive Dow lost 1.2% while the growth-heavy Nasdaq lost 0.2%.
  • The front end is not the story — a hike on 10/28 is priced below 10%, so the long end is doing all the work; 5.00% on the 10Y is October's line in the sand.
  • This is a risk premium, not a shortage: Brent at $116.72 with Hormuz flows still near prewar levels can fade on a headline, which is exactly why it is dangerous to be short volatility into the weekend.
  • Next week is the calendar, not the tape: FOMC 10/27-28, PCE 10/29 and the Alphabet-Microsoft-Amazon block, with the S&P 2.50% below its record and October at -0.36%.

chains.t: ① The Oil Price Became the Discount Rate: $116.72 Brent, 59.8 Selling Prices, a 5.00% 10Y
steps: Iran-backed Houthis claimed strikes on the Yanbu oil-loading port, an Aramco site and the Dammam and Abha airports over 48 hours, with two killed at Dammam; Saudi Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters on 10/22

The Wall Street Journal reported that Tehran has told Washington and Gulf states it will hit airports, pipelines and telecoms in neighbouring countries if US-Israeli air operations resume — the threat moved from military to civilian infrastructure
Brent's December contract settled $3.55 (3.1%) higher at $116.72, its highest close since 29 April, after a $117.45 session high; WTI settled $3.80 (3.8%) higher at $103.27
The October flash composite PMI slipped to 57.6 from 58.4, but its selling-price index rose to 59.8 — the fastest since August 2022 — and new orders hit 58.2, the highest since March 2022
The rate read: the 10Y gave back 4bp of Thursday's 17bp rally to 5.00%, and the 2Y and 30Y each rose 4bp to 4.69% and 5.33% — a parallel move, not a haven bid
The bill: energy +2.60% and tech +0.49% were the only sectors with a gain worth the name, while staples -1.92%, communication services -1.78% and financials -1.32% carried the losses
chains.d: The chain: a wider war premium plus four-year-high selling prices put the long end back at 5%, and the bill was paid by the yield-sensitive half of the index while the barrel's own sector rallied.

news.fact: Houthi rebels claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia's Defence Ministry, two airports and an Aramco facility in Yanbu over 48 hours; two people died and several were injured in attacks at Dammam airport, and Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters, the first such evacuation since the Iran war began.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Iran has warned it will expand its attacks beyond US bases and warships to airports, oil and gas pipelines and telecommunications infrastructure in neighbouring Gulf states if American and Israeli strikes resume.

Brent crude futures settled at $116.72 a barrel, up $3.55 or 3.14%, their highest since April 29; US West Texas Intermediate closed at $103.27 a barrel, up $3.80 or 3.8%. Brent finished the week up 6% and WTI 2.3% higher.
Brent's session high of $117.45 was its highest in nearly six months.
The flash US Composite PMI Output Index fell to 57.6 in October from 58.4, while the output-prices index rose to 59.8 — the highest reading since August 2022 — and input costs were 64.9 against 65.9.
Selling prices rose at the sharpest rate since August 2022, with S&P Global saying the pace indicates consumer price inflation is likely to rise further above the Fed's target in the coming months.
The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.00% versus 4.96% the prior session, the 2-year at 4.69% versus 4.65% and the 30-year at 5.33% versus 5.29%, per the Treasury's daily yield curve.

Stocks fell on the final day of a volatile trading week Friday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average shedding 650 points; the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Dow 1.2% on the day, while energy rose 2.5% and information technology 0.5%.

chains.t: ② The Tech Floor: Memory Bounced and the Nasdaq Lost Only 0.2%
steps: The iShares Semiconductor ETF rose 0.53% after Thursday's 6.5% slide, and the Roundhill Memory ETF gained 3.0% after a 7% plunge
SK Hynix rose 4.1% after the South Korean company ended plans for a US public offering of its Solidigm subsidiary
Micron +2.5%, AMD +1.7%, Intel +1.7% and Microsoft +0.7%: the names that led Thursday's rout stopped falling on Friday
The AI platforms did not join: Meta fell another 1.0% to $642.62 and Nvidia slipped 0.6%, so the bid was in hardware and memory rather than in the capex owners
The index arithmetic: the Dow fell 1.23% while the Nasdaq fell 0.20% — on this session the cyclical index, not the AI complex, was the weak side
chains.d: The cap on the day: the AI complex found a bid in memory and semis, which is why an oil shock of this size cost the Nasdaq two-tenths of a point and the Dow more than a full one.

news.fact: Memory and other AI-tied stocks rebounded after selling off Thursday: Roundhill's Memory ETF rose 3% following a 7% plunge, SK Hynix gained 4% after ending plans for a US public offering of its Solidigm subsidiary, and the broader iShares Semiconductor ETF was 0.5% higher following a roughly 6.5% drop.

Several AI-related companies rallied, helping ease some of the impact from the broader market slide: Micron Technology rose 2.5%, Intel gained 1.7%, Microsoft added 0.7% and Advanced Micro Devices closed 1.7% higher.
The Dow Industrials and S&P 500 fell on Friday while technology shares steadied to end a turbulent week for the market-driving AI trade.

chains.t: ③ The Dow's 653-Point Hole: AmEx, Caterpillar and a Satellite Carrier
steps: American Express fell 3.68% to $313.22 despite beating estimates — it announced its first major job cuts in roughly a decade — and peers followed: JPMorgan -1.47%, Citigroup -1.5%, Capital One -1.0%
Caterpillar -2.42%, Goldman Sachs -1.75% and Home Depot -2.41%: those three plus AmEx accounted for roughly 320 of the Dow's 653 points

Telecoms were re-rated on competition: AT&T closed 8.0% lower and T-Mobile 7.7% after Bloomberg reported SpaceX is in talks for at least 80,000 US cell sites, while Crown Castle rose 9.1% and American Tower 4.1%
Staples was the worst sector, with Procter & Gamble -2.76%, Coca-Cola -2.76%, Colgate -3.44% and Hormel -3.42% — one session after the group stood at +11.65% MTD
The breadth: 24 of the 30 Dow components fell and nearly three of every four S&P 500 stocks declined, with the equal-weight RSP -0.77% against the S&P's -0.52%
chains.d: The split: the oil-and-rates bill was charged to the price-weighted, cyclical-heavy Dow, while the Nasdaq's semis found a floor.

news.fact: US telecom stocks declined after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier; AT&T fell 5.6% to a more than three-month low, Verizon lost 1.6% and T-Mobile shed 5%.
Shares of cell-tower firms Crown Castle and American Tower surged a respective 9.5% and 4%, while those of major mobile providers AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile were down 1.5% to 7.5%.

American Express slumped 3.7%, one of several financial stocks that lost ground, despite reporting profits that beat analysts' forecasts; the company also announced its first major job cuts in roughly a decade. JPMorgan fell 1.5%, Citigroup 1.5% and Capital One 1%. Rising oil prices weighed on a market where nearly three out of every four stocks in the S&P 500 fell.

chains.t: ④ What Didn't Break: a Third Straight Weekly Gain for the Dow
steps: The week: the Dow +0.4%, its third consecutive weekly gain, against the S&P 500 -0.5% and the Nasdaq -0.7% — a second straight weekly loss for both, but a shallow one
The barrel's own relief valve: crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered to near prewar levels even as futures closed at a six-month high

The policy offsets: the Energy Department authorised an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve for Phillips 66's Lake Charles refinery, and the president said the US could end the war quickly
The rate market's cap: a quarter-point hike at the 10/28 meeting is priced below 10%, so the near-term risk in the tape is the barrel, not the Fed
The earnings floor: 111 S&P 500 companies have reported and 83% have beaten (LSEG), with Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon due 10/26-30
chains.d: The floor: the week still ended with the Dow higher, Hormuz flowing, a 400,000-barrel SPR bridge and a Fed priced to hold — the damage was to the discount rate, not to demand.

news.fact: The Dow ended up 0.4% for the week, its third straight weekly gain, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq finished a respective 0.5% and 0.7% lower over the five sessions — their second straight weekly loss.
The flareup threatens to widen hostilities around the Strait of Hormuz, where crude exports have recovered to near prewar levels.

The US Department of Energy said it had authorized an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address a supply disruption affecting Phillips 66's Lake Charles refinery; President Trump said the US could end the war with Iran quickly.
Traders lowered their bets for another interest rate increase, with the probability of a quarter-point increase at the Federal Reserve's meeting next week currently sitting below 10%.
Third-quarter earnings season is well underway, with 111 of the companies in the S&P 500 having reported; of those, 83% have beaten analyst expectations, according to the most recent LSEG data.

mtd.h: October, Seventeen Sessions In: -0.36% and a 2.50% Drawdown — With Energy +12.7% Taking the Lead
mtd.d: S&P 7,651.5 to 7,623.7 (-0.36% MTD): 2.50% below the 10/6 record, with Energy +12.7% now leading and Tech -6.4% worst — a 19.1-point spread.
mtd.c1: Seventeen sessions into October, the S&P 500 is -0.36% at 7,623.68 — 2.50% below the S&P 500's record close of 7,818.93 on 10/6 — while the Nasdaq is -3.37% and the Dow +2.57%. The month's arc: one record close, three repricings (wireless on 10/9, the AI complex on 10/12-13, the CPI-PPI pair on 10/14-15), a three-session repair from 10/19 to 10/21, and then two down sessions that took the month below zero. The 10Y touched 5.36% on 10/7 and closed at 5.00% (-29bp MTD); the 30Y is -31bp at 5.33%. Beneath the index: Energy +12.73% has taken the lead, Staples +9.50%, Tech -6.40% — a 19.1-point spread — with eight of 11 sectors positive. Oil on the December contract: WTI +16.8%, Brent +19.1%. Gates: FOMC 10/27-28, PCE 10/29.
mtd.c4:
• October is a round trip with a different leader: -0.36% MTD and 2.50% below the 10/6 record, and the month's best sector is now the barrel rather than the pantry.
  • The dispersion trade still pays, but the legs changed: Energy +12.7% against Tech -6.4% is a 19.1-point spread — the defensives that carried the first three weeks gave 1.9 points back on 10/23 alone.
  • The month's last gate is the PCE print on 10/29, the day after the Fed decides; a 5.00% 10Y is the level that decides whether October ends green.
  • Watch the contract, not the headline: WTI +16.8% MTD against Brent +19.1%, both December — the spread says the war premium is in the waterborne barrel, not the American one.

chains.t: ① October's Round Trip: a Record, Three Repricings, One Repair — and Two Down Sessions

Three repricings between 10/7 and 10/15: wireless on 10/9, the AI complex on 10/12-13, and the CPI-PPI pair on 10/14-15, when the index lost 1.11% in a single session

The give-back: 1.21% on 10/22 and 0.52% on 10/23 took 1.7 points off the month and left the index -0.36% MTD, 2.50% below the high
chains.d: October so far: one record, three repricings, one repair and two down sessions — the index is slightly negative and the leadership has changed hands.

news.fact: The S&P 500 closed above 7,800 for the first time — up 0.6% on the day — and the Nasdaq set another record close.
Shares of the country's largest telecommunications giants are slumping amid worries about growing competition from SpaceX.
Chip stocks rallied Monday, on pace to end a nine-day losing streak.

news.fact: Slightly more than half of the stocks in the S&P 500 fell, but all but seven of the 75 stocks in the index's tech sector closed lower.
The S&P 500 value index rose 0.9% compared with a 0.2% drop in its growth counterpart, and the small-cap Russell 2000 finished up 1.7%.
Energy and information technology were the strongest sectors on Friday, rising 2.5% and 0.5%, as the benchmark index fell 0.5% and headed for a losing week.

chains.t: ③ The Barrel, Seventeen Sessions In: $98 to $117
steps: The path: Brent's December contract began October at $98.03, crossed $100 on 10/1, held a $100-107 corridor through 10/15, closed $109.86 on 10/16 and $116.72 on 10/23
The print: a $117.45 session high on 10/23, the highest level in nearly six months

chains.d: October's barrel: supply data capped the premium for three weeks, then the war premium took Brent to $116.72 — a 19% month and a six-month high.

news.fact: US crude stocks fell by 3.06 million barrels to 412.5 million barrels last week, compared with analysts' expectations for an 820,000-barrel draw.
Crude and condensate flows from the Persian Gulf hit a high of 24.6 million barrels a day in the week to Oct. 18, according to Kpler, though October so far averages 16.7 million.
Brent crude futures settled at $116.72 a barrel, up 3.14%, their highest since April 29; WTI closed at $103.27, up 3.8%.

qtd.h: Q4's Opening Ledger: -0.36% Banked, a 5.36% Print — and Every Gate Still Ahead
qtd.d: From 9/30's 7,651.5 to 7,623.7 (-0.36% QTD): one record, one yield spike, three AI repricings, and none of the quarter's verdicts in.
qtd.c1: Q4 is seventeen sessions old and has nothing to show for it: the S&P sits at 7,623.68, -0.36% on the quarter, with the Nasdaq -3.37% and the Dow +2.57%. Against a +2.0% third quarter, the fourth has given back everything it made between 10/1 and 10/9. What is in the ledger: a record close of 7,818.93 on 10/6; a 24-year high of 5.36% on the 10Y on 10/7, now 5.00% — a net -29bp; three AI de-ratings; and a 19.1% quarterly rise in Brent that has re-priced the inflation path. What is not: the FOMC on 10/27-28, PCE and advance Q3 GDP on 10/29, the megacap earnings week that starts 10/26, and the 11/3 midterms. The quarter's test is whether -0.36% survives five weeks of gates.
qtd.c4:
• The quarter has banked a record and a 24-year yield print, not a direction — the S&P is 2.50% below its 10/6 high with all four big gates unplayed.
  • Position for the calendar, not the tape: the Fed, PCE, the Alphabet-Microsoft-Amazon earnings week and the midterms all land inside the next eight trading days.
  • The rate bill is the swing: a 5.00% 10Y on 10/23 is 36bp below the 10/7 peak; if that holds, the AI complex keeps a valuation cushion it did not have for most of October.
  • The quarter's oil bill is already visible in the inflation data: four-year-high selling prices with $116.72 Brent is the combination that keeps the long end from rallying for the right reason.

chains.t: ① The Ledger: What Q4 Banked and What It Still Owes
steps: Banked: a 7,818.93 all-time closing high on 10/6, the quarter's only one
Banked: a 24-year high of 5.36% on the 10Y on 10/7, and a 5.00% close on 10/23 — a net -29bp for the quarter
Banked: three de-ratings of the AI complex, all inside the first eleven trading days
Owed: the policy verdict — the FOMC meets 10/27-28 with a quarter-point hike priced below 10%
Owed: the earnings verdict — 83% of the 111 S&P companies reported have beaten, but three of the four biggest data-center spenders have not reported
The standing: -0.36% QTD against a +2.0% third quarter — the quarter has kept none of the summer's momentum
chains.d: Q4's first seventeen sessions banked a record and a yield spike, then handed the gain back — the verdict sits with the Fed and the AI earnings week.

news.fact: The S&P 500 closed above 7,800 for the first time — up 0.6% on the day — and the Nasdaq set another record close.
Third-quarter earnings season is well underway, with 111 of the companies in the S&P 500 having reported; of those, 83% have beaten analyst expectations, according to the most recent LSEG data.
Traders lowered their bets for another interest rate increase, with the probability of a quarter-point increase at the Federal Reserve's meeting next week currently sitting below 10%.

chains.t: ② The Quarter's Rate Bill: From 5.36% to 5.00% in Seventeen Sessions
steps: The 10Y opened Q4 at 5.29%, printed 5.36% on 10/7 and closed 10/23 at 5.00% — a net -29bp
The curve came in together: the 30Y is -31bp on the quarter at 5.33% and the 2Y -19bp at 4.69%
The cost: more than $5 billion of US and European debt sales were postponed in October, the biggest spate of delays this year
The mirror: France's 10Y above 5% with the OAT-Bund spread near a 15-year high of 160bp — the term-premium squeeze is global
The offset: the 10Y's -29bp and Brent's +19.1% landed in the same quarter — duration was bought alongside a rising barrel, not against it
chains.d: The quarter's rate bill: a 10Y that touched 5.36% and has since given back 29bp — relief bought with a growth scare, not with disinflation.

news.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.00% versus 5.29% at the end of September, the 2-year at 4.69% versus 4.88% and the 30-year at 5.33% versus 5.64%, per the Treasury's daily yield curve.
Companies have postponed more than $5 billion in US and European debt sales this month across at least seven companies, the biggest spate of postponements this year.
France's 10-year bond yield hit a new 24-year high above 5%, and the premium on French yields over German Bunds edged back toward a 15-year high of nearly 160 bps.

chains.t: ③ The Quarter's Calendar: Four Verdicts Before the Midterms
steps: 10/27-28: the FOMC, with the 10Y at 5.00% and a hike priced below 10%
10/29: PCE and the first estimate of Q3 GDP, one day after the meeting
10/26-30: Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon report — the capex question at index scale
11/3: the midterms, the quarter's last political date
After 11/3: the December meeting and the November inflation print decide whether -0.36% is a base or a peak
chains.d: Q4's next four verdicts — Fed, PCE, megacap earnings, midterms — decide whether -0.36% is a base or a peak.

news.fact: Alphabet Inc., Microsoft Corp. and Amazon.com Inc., three of the other biggest spenders on data centers, are slated to report next week.
Personal Income and Outlays for September, which carries the PCE price index, and the advance estimate of third-quarter GDP are both scheduled for October 29 at 8:30 a.m.

ytd.h: The Bull at +11.37%: AI Earnings Carry, an 82bp Rate Bill
ytd.d: S&P +11.37%, Nasdaq +11.67%, Dow +8.64% — AI capex and earnings carry; a 10Y up 82bp, a $117 barrel and a 7.7% gold drawdown tax the rest.
ytd.c1: The year's base case still holds: AI capex and earnings carry the S&P to +11.37% (7,623.68) and the Nasdaq to +11.67%, with the Dow +8.64%; the bull turned four on 10/12. Against it: a 10Y at 5.00% (+82bp YTD), Brent +91.8% and WTI +79.9% since 12/31 as the war grinds into an eighth month, and a hot September CPI (3.7%) and PPI (6.3%). Beneath the index: Energy +55.1% leads the year, Tech +27.3%, Health +15.8%; Comms -10.4% and ConsDisc -5.3% lag, while Utilities are -0.3%. Gold -7.7%, bitcoin -7.1%, the dollar +3.6%. The S&P is 2.50% below its record; the Nasdaq is 5.96% below its 10/6 record close.
ytd.c4:
• The year's engine is intact: AI capex and 29% earnings growth have carried the S&P +11.37% through an 82bp rise in the 10Y — earnings are doing the work rates used to do.
  • The dispersion is the year's signature: Energy +55.1% against Comms -10.4% is a 65.4-point spread — the index's +11.37% is an average of two very different markets.
  • The year's last macro gate is December: a pause this month is priced, and the December decision is where the bull's 2027 setup gets set.
  • The barrel is the year's biggest swing factor: Brent +91.8% has put four-year-high selling prices into the October survey, which is why 5.00% on the 10Y looks more like a resting point than a peak.

steps: The engines: AI capex across the hyperscalers and earnings, with Q3 growth tracking 29%
The scoreboard: S&P +11.37%, Nasdaq +11.67%, Dow +8.64% — the AI-heavy index leads by 30bp rather than by points
The referee: the 10Y at 5.00%, +82bp YTD, down from a 24-year high of 5.36% printed on 10/7
The taxes: WTI +79.9% and Brent +91.8% since 12/31 as the war grinds into an eighth month; September CPI 3.7% and PPI 6.3%
The margin: the S&P is 2.50% off its record and the Nasdaq 5.96% off its 10/6 close — a bull with a valuation discount, not a broad one
chains.d: The year's base case: AI and earnings compound, rates and oil tax — a four-year bull still faster than its referee.

news.fact: The bull market turned four on Monday, with many strategists expecting more room for stocks to run.
Analysts are forecasting overall growth of 29% for companies in the S&P 500 from the prior summer.
The Dow and S&P 500 fell on Friday while technology shares steadied; the S&P 500 is up 11% this year, the Nasdaq 12% and the Dow 9%, according to the close.

chains.t: ② The Rate and Inflation Tax
steps: The long end: the 10Y from 4.18% to 5.00% (+82bp); the 30Y from 4.84% to 5.33% (+49bp)
The Fed: a September hike, its first since July 2023, with a hold priced for 10/28 and the December meeting the live one
The prints: September CPI 3.7% y/y and PPI 6.3% y/y, and October's flash selling-price index at 59.8 — the highest since August 2022
The cross-asset echo: the dollar +3.6% and gold -7.7% — real rates, not war, are setting the tone for both
The global mirror: France's 10Y above 5% for the first time since 2002 — a term-premium problem that is not only American
chains.d: 2026's tax: an 82bp rise in the 10Y and a second inflation wave — the September hike was the year's regime change.

news.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.00% versus 4.18% at the end of 2025, and the 30-year at 5.33% versus 4.84%, per the Treasury's daily yield curve.
Selling prices rose at the sharpest rate since August 2022, a pace that S&P Global said indicates consumer price inflation is likely to rise further above the Fed's target in the coming months.
France's 10-year bond yield hit a new 24-year high above 5%, and the premium on French yields over German Bunds edged back toward a 15-year high of nearly 160 bps.

chains.t: ③ The Year's Two Markets: Energy +55%, Comms -10% — a 65-Point Spread
steps: The leader is the barrel: Energy +55.07% for the year, with December crude at $116.72
The laggard is communication services at -10.37%, where the wireless carriers have been re-rated twice this year on SpaceX's carrier ambitions
The spread is 65.4 points; the S&P's +11.37% is the average of those two markets
The middle is defensive: Health +15.8%, Staples +13.6% and Materials +13.1%, while Utilities are -0.3% — pricing power, not bond-proxy duration, is what paid
The auditor: a 10Y at 5.00% (+82bp YTD) decides which half of that spread gets paid
chains.d: The year in one line: the barrel and the pantry beat the platform, and the 10Y decides the size of the check.

news.fact: Energy shares were lifted by rising crude prices, with SLB and Halliburton up 6.5% and 5%, while communication services was the weakest S&P 500 sector on the day.
US telecom stocks declined after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier; AT&T fell to a more than three-month low and T-Mobile shed 5%.
Brent is up more than 85% this year because of the US-Iran war, which is now approaching its ninth month.
